title: The Garden Pond
assumptions: Reeds and pond plants are imagined as the growers
Snails and insects are guessed visitors, not seen
Fish and dragonflies are playful guesses
A teaching model, not a real survey; three animal groups are curated guesses.
The pond uses a reviewed open-water rectangle, not a measured shoreline.
landscape: rocky pond bank with pale boulders and pebbles, grassy mounds and piney hill behind

inhabitants.name: Pond Reeds
inhabitants.look: tall spiky tufts of green reeds

inhabitants.name: Pond Snail
inhabitants.look: small brown spiral shell with soft body

inhabitants.name: Pond Dragonfly
inhabitants.look: shiny blue darting wings over water

inhabitants.name: Pond Goldfish
inhabitants.look: An imagined small orange goldfish with flowing fins

events.title: What if it rains less?
events.why: Less rain means less water for growing food.

events.title: What if a warm spell lasts?
events.why: In our teaching rules, warmth uses more water.

events.title: What if another Pond Snail joins?
events.why: More plant-eaters share the same food.
